Reflection summary:

What happened: The two Hazen reference files already contained the exact correct method AND the correct gold answer (678077.00), with a fully worked example showing n=10 → p₉=0.85 exactly → 9th-smallest value, no interpolation. So this was NOT a knowledge gap. The run still emitted 732852.00, which is the MAXIMUM (FY2020, rank 10 = the 95th Hazen percentile, not the 85th). The agent grabbed the max instead of the second-largest.

What I saved (generalizable):
1. Patched references/hazen-plotting-position-percentile.md with a HARD GATE at the top: for n=10, the 85th Hazen percentile is rank 9 = second-largest, never the max. It explicitly names the wrong value (732852 = the max) vs gold (678077), and gives a one-line sanity check: the answer must be strictly less than max(set). If your candidate equals the largest value, you used the np.percentile default or grabbed the max — back off to rank 9.
2. Memory: condensed an existing entry to fit a pointer to this gate so a future run flags the "candidate == max" failure mode before submitting.

This is worth saving because it's a self-check that catches the specific, recurring failure (returning the max for an 85th-percentile-of-10 question) even when the method text is correct — the gate converts knowledge into a verifiable guardrail.
